newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close up, short of all-time high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close up, short of all-time high.

text.p: French shares closed with a big gain on Tuesday but remained below an all-time intra-day high.
Shares were boosted by a strong gain on Wall Street on Monday night and on new opinion polls showing a lead for the ruling centre-right majority.
The blue-chip index came at 2,732.94 within four points of its all-time high -- 2,736.71 on March 11 -- but after U.S. retail sales data and a lower Wall Street opening, profit-taking pulled it back.
The CAC-40 index closed up 26.49 points or 0.98 percent at 2,719.58 for a fresh closing high since March 10, 1997.
The May future was 25.5 points higher at 2,709.
Volume was a high 10.27 billion francs with dealers noting U.S. and British investment funds on the buying side.
Oil stocks such as Elf-Aquitaine, up 1.20 percent at 588 francs, and Total, up 3.39 percent at 519 francs, were boosted by higher oil prices.

Index heavyweight Alcatel Alsthom gained 3.57 percent to 668 francs on the back of first quarter sales, which were 12.1 percent higher. It outlined its plans for buying Thomson-CSF, reiterating it would not lead to excessive debt.
Alcatel chairman Serge Tchuruk said that he was surprised by the market's reaction to the sales figures while admitting an increase in orders for the telecoms sector was very important.

"It shows we are on the road to recovery. There is still a long way to go but we are on the right track," he told Reuters. "I'm surprised that the market is surprised when we announce that we are doing things that we said we would," he added.

Lagardere, the rival in bidding for the state's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF, saw its shares slip 0.54 percent to 184.10 franc. Lagardere placed five billion francs in convertible bonds with investors.
